dervis-irab:1-6.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَعْزُبُ): In al-Miṣbāḥ: «عزب الشيء, of the patterns qatala and ḍaraba: it was absent and hidden». In al-Asās: «One says: عزب عنه حلمه, and أعزب حلمه, as you say أضل بعيره [he lost his camel]; أعزب الله عقلك (may Allah make your mind go far away); a remote meadow (rawḍ ʿāzib and ʿazīb); camels pastured far away (māl ʿazab) and pastured out (jashar). Remote pasture (al-kalaʾ al-ʿāzib) is only in a desert where there is no cultivation. So-and-so is a miʿzāb and miʿzāba, said of one who goes far off with his camels. One says عزب ظهر المرأة when [her husband] is absent. Among borrowed usages is the saying of al-Nābigha:
وصدر أراح الليل عازب همه ... تضاعف فيه الحزن من كل جانب
(A breast to which the night brought back its far-straying care, in which grief has multiplied from every side.)
You may say امرأة عزبة (an unmarried woman). Al-miʿzāba is one whose bachelorhood has been long and prolonged. One says: so-and-so has no wife تعذبه [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense requires تعزبه], i.e. who would take away his bachelorhood». In al-Qāmūs:
«Al-ʿazab, with fatḥas, is one who has no family, like al-miʿzāba and al-ʿazīb; do not say aʿzab, or [say it] rarely; its plural is aʿzāb; [the feminine] is ʿazaba and ʿazab; the noun is al-ʿuzba and al-ʿuzūba, with two ḍammas; the verb is like naṣara. تعزّب: he abandoned marriage. Al-ʿuzūb is absence — يعزُب and يعزِب — and going away». Among the remarkable features of ʿayn and zāy is that when they are the first and second radicals of a word, they indicate the meaning of going away, remoteness, isolation and overpowering. In the ḥadīth: «Whoever reads the Qurʾān in forty nights عزّب», i.e. he has put a long time since [reading] its beginning. عز الرجل: he became ʿazīz (mighty), i.e. far removed from others by his qualities, until he rose above them. عز الشيء: it became scarce, so that it is hardly found. عز عليّ أن أسوءك: [it is hard for me to grieve you], i.e. it is severe and overpowering. You say to a man: "Do you love me?" and he says: "لعزّما and لشدّما" (how intensely!). استعزّ به المرض: the illness overpowered him and grew severe. تعزز لحم الناقة: the she-camel's flesh became firm and hard. «فعززنا بثالث», i.e. We strengthened [them]. عزّز بهم: he was strict with them and granted no concession; from this is the ḥadīth of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him: some people shared in [killing] a game animal and said to him: "Is there a compensation on each one of us, or one compensation?" He said: "Then you would be treated strictly! Rather, upon you is one compensation." عزف عن الشيء: he loathed it and renounced it. Al-ʿazf is the sound of the winds and of the tambourine. You say: the striking of musical instruments (maʿāzif) distracted so-and-so from the kinds of renunciation (maʿāzif); and I travelled a desert in which the jinn have a humming (ʿazīf). عزله يعزله, of the pattern ḍaraba, from such-and-such: he removed him from it; عزل فلانا عن منصبه: he removed and dismissed him from his post. You say: why do I see you aloof (fī maʿzil) from your companions? and I am apart (bi-maʿzil) from this matter; I kept away from falsehood (اعتزلت and تعزلته). Al-Aḥwaṣ said:
يا بيت عاتكة الذي أتعزل ... حذر العدا وبه الفؤاد موكل
(O house of ʿĀtika, which I avoid for fear of enemies, while the heart is devoted to it.)
I seek refuge in Allah from the aʿzal on an aʿzal, i.e. from a man who has no weapon with him, on a horse with a crooked tail-bone, so that it inclines its tail to one side. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
ضليع إذا استدبرته سدّ فرجه ... بضاف فويق الأرض ليس بأعزل
(Stout of rib; when you view him from behind, he fills the gap between his legs with an abundant tail just above the ground, not crooked.)
اعتزم الفرس في عنانه: when the horse goes on headstrong without turning. He said:
سبوح إذا اعتزمت في العنان ... مروح ململمة كالحجر
(A swift-running mare when she presses on in the rein, lively, compact like a stone.)
عزمت على الأمر and اعتزمت عليه [I resolved on the matter], and that only comes from firmness and mastery. He is ʿizhāh regarding amusement and women when he does not desire them and keeps far from them. He said: إذا كنت عزهاة عن اللهو والصبا ... فكن حجرا من يابس الصخر جلمدا
(If you are averse to amusement and youthful passion, then be a stone, a hard boulder of dry rock.)
عزا الشيء or so-and-so to so-and-so: he attributed it and traced it back to him. Indeed so-and-so is attributed to goodness (yuʿzā and yaʿtazī). This ḥadīth is attributed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I saw them around him ʿizīn, i.e. in groups. This is among the secrets of our noble language.
(رِجْزٍ): with kasra or ḍamma on the rāʾ: punishment, or the worst of it; sin, offence and filth.

* I'rab:
(الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي لَهُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ): الحمد is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and لله its khabar (predicate); الذي is a naʿt (adjective); له is a fronted khabar and ما a postponed mubtadaʾ; في السموات is the ṣila (relative clause), and ما في الأرض is conjoined to ما في السموات.
(وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ): the wāw is a conjunction; له is a fronted khabar and الحمد a postponed mubtadaʾ; في الآخرة is a ḥāl (circumstantial); هو is a mubtadaʾ, الحكيم a first khabar and الخبير a second khabar.
(يَعْلَمُ ما يَلِجُ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَما يَخْرُجُ مِنْها): you may make it a predicative clause, so that it is a third khabar of هو, as though it details some of the matters encompassed by His knowledge, the Exalted, relating to the religious and worldly interests of His servants. You may make it an emphatic ḥāl, and you may make it resumptive, introduced to confirm what preceded. يعلم is a nominative imperfect verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "هو", referring to Allah the Exalted. ما is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause يلج is the ṣila; في الأرض is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يلج; وما يخرج is conjoined to ما يلج في الأرض.
(وَما يَنْزِلُ مِنَ السَّماءِ وَما يَعْرُجُ فِيها وَهُوَ الرَّحِيمُ الْغَفُورُ):
conjoined to what precedes. Ascending (al-ʿurūj) was made to include the sense of settling, so it was made transitive with في rather than إلى.
(وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لا تَأْتِينَا السَّاعَةُ قُلْ بَلى وَرَبِّي لَتَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ): the wāw is resumptive; قال الذين is a verb and its fāʿil; the clause كفروا is the ṣila. لا is negative; تأتينا الساعة is an imperfect verb, a mafʿūl bihi and a fāʿil. قل is an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "أنت". بلى is a particle of answer that affirms [the opposite of] the negation, i.e. the matter is nothing other than its coming. وربي: the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive, and ربي is genitive by the wāw of the oath. He emphasised the affirmation against the negation with what is the utmost in emphasis and intensity, namely the oath by Allah, Mighty and Majestic. The lām is the answer to the oath; تأتينكم is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi, and this is a third emphasis.
(عالِمِ الْغَيْبِ لا يَعْزُبُ عَنْهُ مِثْقالُ ذَرَّةٍ فِي السَّماواتِ وَلا فِي الْأَرْضِ): عالم is an adjective of ربي, or a badal (substitute). It may be nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, or as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause لا يعزب; it has been read in both ways. The clause لا يعزب is either a khabar or a ḥāl. عنه is attached to يعزب; مثقال ذرة is the fāʿil; في السموات is a ḥāl; ولا في الأرض is conjoined to في السموات.
(وَلا أَصْغَرُ مِنْ ذلِكَ وَلا أَكْبَرُ إِلَّا فِي كِتابٍ مُبِينٍ): the wāw is a conjunction and لا is negative. أصغر من ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, and من ذلك is a khabar [Translator's note: so in the source, which then gives في كتاب مبين as the khabar of أصغر; من ذلك is presumably meant to be attached to أصغر]. ولا أكبر is conjoined to ولا أصغر; إلا is a particle of restriction; في كتاب مبين is the khabar of أصغر. You may also make the speech continuous, conjoining ولا أصغر to مثقال, so that في كتاب is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; but the first is preferable.
(لِيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ أُولئِكَ لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَرِزْقٌ كَرِيمٌ): ليجزي: the lām is causal; يجزي is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تأتينكم, as though it were a reason for, and an explanation of, what its coming entails; or to His words لا يعزب, as though He said: He counts that so as to recompense. الذين is a mafʿūl bihi; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila of الذين; عملوا الصالحات is conjoined to آمنوا. أولئك is a mubtadaʾ, لهم a fronted khabar and مغفرة a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the khabar of أولئك. رزق is conjoined to مغفرة, and كريم is an adjective.
(وَالَّذِينَ سَعَوْا فِي آياتِنا مُعاجِزِينَ أُولئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذابٌ مِنْ رِجْزٍ أَلِيمٌ): the wāw is either a conjunction, so that الذين is conjoined to what precedes, i.e. and [that] He may recompense those who strove; or it may be resumptive, so that الذين is a mubtadaʾ. The clause سعوا is the ṣila; في آياتنا is attached to سعوا, with a muḍāf implied, i.e. in invalidating Our signs by attacking them, or describing them as sorcery, poetry and the like. معاجزين is a ḥāl. Al-Rāghib said: «The root meaning of al-ʿajz is lagging behind, because the one lagging behind is behind the rump (ʿajuz) of the one ahead, or near it; then it became customary in what is commonly known. What is meant here by al-muʿājaza is the lagging behind that is preceded by the advance of the one ahead. The meaning of mutuality is not intended here, since what is intended is outstripping and others' inability to overcome them, owing to their supremacy». [Translator's note: the closing of al-Rāghib's quotation is not marked in the source; what follows may be the author's comment.] All of that is based on their corrupt claims and imagined fancies. أولئك is a mubtadaʾ, لهم a fronted khabar and عذاب a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive on the first view, or the khabar of الذين on the second. من رجز is an adjective of عذاب and أليم a second adjective.
(وَيَرَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ هُوَ الْحَقَّ): ويرى is in the position of the nominative, as being resumptive, or in the position of the accusative, being conjoined to يجزي. الذين is the fāʿil of يرى; the clause أوتوا العلم is the ṣila; الذي is the first object of يرى, because it is [a verb] of the heart; the clause أنزل is the ṣila; إليك is attached to أنزل; من ربك is a ḥāl, or is also attached to أنزل. هو is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position, and الحق is the second object of يرى.
(وَيَهْدِي إِلى صِراطِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ): ويهدي is conjoined to الحق; the conjunction is permissible because the verb is interpreted as a noun, as if it were said: "and guiding". You may make the wāw circumstantial and the clause in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, and it may be resumptive. The fāʿil of يهدي is a latent pronoun referring to الذي أنزل إليك; إلى صراط is attached to يهدي; العزيز is the muḍāf ilayhi of صراط, and الحميد is a naʿt.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words «الحمد لله», expression by a nominal clause conveys continuity and permanence. Ḥamd (praise) linguistically is describing [someone] by a voluntary excellence with the intent of glorifying. Description is only by the tongue, so its source is specific; and this description may be in return for a favour or otherwise, so its object is general. Linguistic shukr (thanks) is the reverse, since it is an action signalling the glorification of the benefactor inasmuch as he has conferred a favour on the one thanking; so its source is the tongue, the heart and the limbs, and its object is the favour reaching the one thanking. So each of them is more general and more specific than the other in one respect: for virtues there is ḥamd only; for acts of the heart and the limbs there is shukr only; and for the act of the tongue in return for a favour there is both ḥamd and shukr.
2- Is thanking the benefactor obligatory or not?
The Ashʿarīs said: thanking the benefactor is not obligatory at all, and they illustrated it with a parable, saying: its likeness is only that of a poor man who attended the table of a great king who owns the lands east and west, and covers the lands with gifts and spoils, and he gave him a morsel of bread in charity; then the poor man began mentioning him in gatherings and thanking him for it by constantly moving his fingertip for his sake. This would be counted as mockery of the king. So it is here; indeed the morsel, relative to the king and what he owns, is more than what Allah has bestowed on the servant relative to Allah, and the servant's thanks is of less worth beside Allah than the poor man's thanks by moving his fingers. The Muʿtazila said: the parable that fits the case is to say: if there were, in a corner of obscurity and an abyss of oblivion, a man mute of tongue, paralysed in hands and feet, deprived of hearing and sight — indeed of all the external senses and the internal faculties — and the king brought him out of that abyss and was kind to him, loosening his tongue, removing the paralysis of his limbs, granting him the senses for gaining benefits and warding off harms, and raising his rank above many of his followers and servants; and then that man, after those great favours had reached him and those honours had poured over him, turned away from thanking that king and ignored him, and nothing appeared from him that signalled any concern, making no distinction between their presence and absence — then there is no doubt that he is blameworthy by every tongue, deserving of humiliation and abandonment.

dervis-irab:7-9.t:
* I'rab:
(وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا: هَلْ نَدُلُّكُمْ عَلى رَجُلٍ يُنَبِّئُكُمْ إِذا مُزِّقْتُمْ كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ): the wāw is resumptive; قال الذين is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause), i.e. some of them said to others. هل is an interrogative particle; ندلكم is an imperfect verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); على رجل is attached (mutaʿalliq) to ندلكم, and what is meant by it is Muḥammad ﷺ; the secret of its being indefinite will come in the Rhetoric section. The clause ينبئكم is an adjective of رجل. إذا is an adverb of the future, attached to an omitted verb whose implied form is "you will be resurrected" or "you will be gathered as a new creation". It is not permissible to attach it to ينبئكم, because the informing does not take place at that time; nor to مزقتم, because it is the muḍāf ilayhi, and the muḍāf ilayhi does not govern the muḍāf; nor to جديد, because إن and the lām of inception prevent that, since both of them must come first; moreover, the adjective does not govern what comes before the qualified noun. Nor is it acceptable to say: suppose it is free of the conditional sense, so that it needs no apodosis and is governed by what precedes it, namely قال, ندلكم or ينبئكم; for these verbs do not occur at the time of tearing apart, so إذا cannot be an adverb for them, since this is not said to them after they are torn apart, but rather occurred while they were alive. A man of the disbelievers would say to his companions, mocking the Prophet ﷺ: "Shall I show you a man… etc." مزقتم is a passive past verb and the tāʾ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). كل ممزق is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because كل takes the status of what it is annexed to, and it has been annexed to ممزق, which is a mīm-maṣdar meaning tearing apart (tamzīq). Al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be a noun of place. He said: «If you ask: you have made al-mumazzaq a maṣdar, as in the verse of al-Kitāb [of Sībawayh]:
ألم تعلم مسرحي القوافي ... فلا عيابهن ولا اجتلابا
(Do you not know my letting loose of rhymes, without faltering in them and without borrowing them?)
— may it then be a place? I say: yes, and its meaning is what ended up in the bellies of birds, what the torrents passed over and carried off in every direction, and what the wind blew away and cast in every place». On this view, كل is an adverb of place.
(إِنَّكُمْ لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ): إن and what follows it stand in place of the two objects of ينبئكم. Its hamza takes kasra only because the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) enters its khabar (predicate). إن and its noun; the emphasising shifted lām; في خلق is the khabar of إن, and جديد is an adjective of خلق; it is faʿīl in the sense of the active participle, and it is said in the sense of the passive participle.
(أَفْتَرى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً أَمْ بِهِ جِنَّةٌ): the hamza is interrogative, and it made the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) unnecessary for reaching the pronunciation of the vowelless letter. على الله is attached to افترى; كذبا is the object of افترى; أم is a conjunction corresponding to the interrogative hamza; به is a fronted khabar and جنة a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. madness.
(بَلِ الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ فِي الْعَذابِ وَالضَّلالِ الْبَعِيدِ): بل is a particle of conjunction and digression (iḍrāb); الذين is a mubtadaʾ; the clause لا يؤمنون is the ṣila; بالآخرة is attached to يؤمنون; في العذاب is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; الضلال is conjoined to العذاب, and البعيد is a naʿt (adjective) of الضلال. The meaning of this adjective will come in the Rhetoric section.
(أَفَلَمْ يَرَوْا إِلى ما بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَما خَلْفَهُمْ مِنَ السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ): a resumptive statement, introduced to make dreadful what they dared to do and said. The hamza is the interrogative of disapproval, and the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted, implied according to the context, i.e. have they become blind, so that they have not seen? Or the hamza is placed before the conjunction; this has been established before. لم is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive; يروا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil. إلى ما is attached to يروا; the adverb is attached to an omitted [verb that forms the] ṣila of ما; أيديهم is the muḍāf ilayhi; وما خلفهم is conjoined to ما بين أيديهم; من السماء is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and الأرض is conjoined to السماء.
(إِنْ نَشَأْ نَخْسِفْ بِهِمُ الْأَرْضَ أَوْ نُسْقِطْ عَلَيْهِمْ كِسَفاً مِنَ السَّماءِ): إن is conditional; نشأ is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and نخسف its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); بهم is attached to نخسف; الأرض is a mafʿūl bihi; أو is a conjunction; نسقط is conjoined to نخسف; عليهم is attached to نسقط; كسفا is a mafʿūl bihi, and من السماء is an adjective of كسفا.
(إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآيَةً لِكُلِّ عَبْدٍ مُنِيبٍ): إن is a particle resembling the verb; في ذلك is its fronted khabar; [then] the shifted lām; آية is its postponed noun; لكل عبد is an adjective of آية, and منيب is an adjective of عبد.

* Rhetoric:
Al-majāz al-ʿaqlī (rational/attributive figurative usage) in His words «والضلال البعيد», because remoteness is a description of the one who strays when he goes far from the straight highway; and the deeper he goes in remoteness from it, the deeper he goes in error.

dervis-irab:10-13.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَوِّبِي): an imperative verb from al-taʾwīb and al-awb, i.e. repeat glorification with him, or return with him in glorification, because when it repeats it, it returns in it.
(سابِغاتٍ): wide, ample coats of mail.
(وَقَدِّرْ فِي السَّرْدِ): al-sard is the weaving of mail. In al-Asās he said:
«سرد النعل وغيرها: he stitched it. Al-Shammākh said, describing wild asses:
شككنا باحساء الذناب على هوى ... كما تابعت سرد العنان الخوارز
(They pressed on to the water-holes of al-Dhanāb, following one another to the water, as the stitching-women follow one another in sewing the rein.)
i.e. they followed one another towards the water. He pierced the leather with the misrad and the sirād, which is the awl that has a hole at its tip. سرد الدرع: when he joined the ends of every two rings and riveted them; a coat of mail that is masrūda, and a garment that is musarrad». Abū al-Ṭayyib said, describing his shirt:
مفرشي صهوة الحصان ولكن ... قميصي مسرودة من حديد
(My bed is the horse's back, and my shirt is a woven [coat] of iron.)
Al-masrūda is what is woven of iron, namely coats of mail. The meaning of measuring in the weaving is: do not make the nails thin, so that they come loose, nor thick, so that they split the rings; what is meant is to make the weaving according to the need. Al-Khaṭīb in his tafsīr took an original line. He said: «His words, the Exalted, وقدر في السرد, i.e. you are not commanded to do it as an obligation; it is only earning, and earning is according to need, and the rest of the days and nights are for worship. So measure in that work and do not occupy all your time with earning; rather obtain from it sustenance only». But the context of the discourse makes this interpretation unlikely, because it is concerned with coats of mail, their weaving, their perfection and the measuring of their manufacture.
In al-Mukhtār: «سرد الدرع, i.e. he wove it, which is inserting the rings into one another; one says سرد الدرع سردا, of the pattern naṣara».
(غُدُوُّها): its travelling in the early morning (ghudwa), which is the time between dawn and sunrise. One says: غدا يغدو غدوا: he went in the early morning. It is also used in the sense of "became", so it puts the mubtadaʾ in the nominative and the khabar in the accusative.
(رَواحُها): its travelling at al-rawāḥ, i.e. the evening.
(الْقِطْرِ): with kasra on the qāf: molten copper. The secret of its being called "the spring of al-qiṭr" will come in the Rhetoric section.
(مَحارِيبَ): al-maḥārīb are noble dwellings and buildings, protected from common use. They were called maḥārīb because they are defended and fought over (yuḥārab ʿalayhā). Then [the word] was transferred to the niche in which the imam stands, which is among the things newly introduced in mosques. The singular is miḥrāb.
(تَماثِيلَ): plural of timthāl, which is a fashioned image; or it is what you make and fashion resembling the creation of Allah among beings with souls, and the image. It is related that they made for him two lions at the base of his throne and two vultures above it; when he wished to ascend, the two lions stretched out their forelegs for him, and when he sat, the two vultures shaded him with their wings.
(جِفانٍ): plural of jafna, which is the large bowl.
(كَالْجَوابِ): plural of jābiya, which is the large basin; it was called jābiya because water is collected (yujbā) in it, i.e. gathered (بجمع [Translator's note: so in the source; read يُجمع]). Al-Aʿshā said, praising al-Muḥallaq:
نفى الذم عن آل المحلق جفنة ... كجابية السيح العراقي تفهق
(Blame was driven away from the family of al-Muḥallaq by a bowl like the basin of the Iraqi stream, brimming over.)
Al-jafna is the bowl of tharīd; al-jābiya is the basin that collects water, i.e. gathers it into the basin; al-sayḥ is abundant running water; فهق يفهق, like فرح يفرح: it became wide (اتسح [Translator's note: so in the source; read اتسع]) and full until it overflowed. It is said that a thousand men would sit at one bowl.
(قُدُورٍ راسِياتٍ): al-qudūr is the plural of qidr, with kasra on the qāf, which is a vessel in which one cooks; راسيات: fixed, having legs, not moving from their places.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا داوُدَ مِنَّا فَضْلًا): the wāw is resumptive; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of realisation; آتينا داود is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). منا is attached (mutaʿalliq) to آتينا, or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an adjective of فضلا; فضلا is the second mafʿūl bihi.
(يا جِبالُ أَوِّبِي مَعَهُ وَالطَّيْرَ وَأَلَنَّا لَهُ الْحَدِيدَ): the vocative clause is governed by an omitted verb of saying, i.e. and We said. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be a badal (substitute) of فضلا. يا is a vocative particle; جبال is a vocative, an intended indefinite noun (nakira maqṣūda); أوّبي is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the yāʾ is the fāʿil; معه is an adverb of place attached to أوّبي. الطير is conjoined to the position of جبال, which is accusative; it was also read in the nominative, conjoined to the [vocative's] wording. The rule for what is conjoined to the vocative will come in the Benefits section. ألنّا is conjoined to آتينا; ألنّا is a past verb and its fāʿil; له is attached to ألنّا; الحديد is a mafʿūl bihi.
(أَنِ اعْمَلْ سابِغاتٍ وَقَدِّرْ فِي السَّرْدِ): أن is maṣdarī, interpreted together with what follows as a maṣdar that is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. لأن أعمل [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has اعمل]. Abū al-Baqāʾ chose that it be explicative (mufassira), and al-Jalāl followed him; but this is rejected, because the condition for explicative أن is that it be preceded by something having the meaning of saying without its letters. Some supplied a verb containing the meaning of saying, and said: the implied form is "We commanded him to make". سابغات is an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl bihi, i.e. ample coats of mail; al-sābighāt are the complete, wide ones. قدر is an imperative verb, and في السرد is attached to قدر.
(وَاعْمَلُوا صالِحاً إِنِّي بِما تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ): اعملوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; صالحا is a mafʿūl bihi, or an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. عملوا عملا صالحا [Translator's note: so in the source; read اعملوا عملا صالحا, "do righteous work"]. إن and its noun; بما تعملون is attached to بصير, and بصير is the khabar (predicate) of إن.
(وَلِسُلَيْمانَ الرِّيحَ غُدُوُّها شَهْرٌ وَرَواحُها شَهْرٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; لسليمان is attached to the omitted verb, i.e. and We subjected the wind to Solomon, so الريح is the object of the omitted verb; that is on the reading in the accusative. On the reading in the nominative it is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject) and لسليمان a fronted khabar. The clause غدوها شهر, composed of mubtadaʾ and khabar, is a ḥāl of الريح; it is said to be resumptive. The clause ورواحها شهر is conjoined to it.
(وَأَسَلْنا لَهُ عَيْنَ الْقِطْرِ): conjoined to the implied سخرنا. أسلنا is a past verb and its fāʿil; له is attached to أسلنا; عين القطر is a mafʿūl bihi.
(وَمِنَ الْجِنِّ مَنْ يَعْمَلُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِ): you may attach من الجن to an implied verb whose implied form is "and We subjected to him", so that من is the mafʿūl bihi of the implied verb; or you may make the preposition and its genitive noun a fronted khabar, so that من is a postponed mubtadaʾ. The clause يعمل is the ṣila (relative clause); بين يديه: the adverb is attached to يعمل; بإذن ربه is attached to an omitted ḥāl.
(وَمَنْ يَزِغْ مِنْهُمْ عَنْ أَمْرِنا نُذِقْهُ مِنْ عَذابِ السَّعِيرِ): the wāw is a conjunction; من is a jussive conditional noun and a mubtadaʾ; يزغ is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); منهم is a ḥāl; عن أمرنا is attached to يزغ; نذقه is the protasis [Translator's note: so in the source; نذقه is in fact the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ)]; the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; من عذاب السعير is attached to نذقه.
(يَعْمَلُونَ لَهُ ما يَشاءُ مِنْ مَحارِيبَ وَتَماثِيلَ وَجِفانٍ كَالْجَوابِ وَقُدُورٍ راسِياتٍ): the clause is a badal of يعمل, detailing what was mentioned of their work. له is attached to يعملون; ما is a mafʿūl bihi; the clause يشاء is the ṣila; من محاريب is in the position of a ḥāl of the omitted object of يشاء, i.e. يشاؤه. محاريب is a diptote because it is a plural on the pattern of the ultimate plural (ṣīghat muntahā al-jumūʿ). تماثيل is conjoined to محاريب, and جفان is also conjoined; كالجواب is an adjective of جفان; the yāʾ of الجواب is dropped in the Qurʾānic script. وقدور راسيات is also conjoined.
(اعْمَلُوا آلَ داوُدَ شُكْراً وَقَلِيلٌ مِنْ عِبادِيَ الشَّكُورُ): a resumptive statement, introduced to recount the favour upon the family of David. اعملوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil; آل داود is a vocative from which the vocative particle has been omitted. شكرا is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. for the sake of thanks. It is said to be a maṣdar from the meaning of اعملوا, as if it were said: give thanks with thanksgiving; or [it is accusative] as a ḥāl, i.e. being thankful. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be accusative by اعملوا as a mafʿūl bihi, its meaning being: We have subjected the jinn to you, making for you whatever you wished, so you, make thanks — by way of mushākala (verbal correspondence). The wāw is circumstantial; قليل is a fronted khabar and الشكور a postponed mubtadaʾ; من عبادي is an adjective of قليل.

* Benefits:
What follows the vocative (tābiʿ al-munādā) is of four kinds:
1- What must be accusative, in regard to the position of the vocative: this is where two things are combined: first, that the follower is a naʿt (adjective), a ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) or a tawkīd (emphasis); second, that the follower is a muḍāf without al-.
2- What must be nominative, in regard to the wording of the vocative: this is the follower of أيّ and the follower of the demonstrative.
3- What may be nominative or accusative: this is of two types: first, the adjective in construct that is joined with al-; second, what is single (not in construct), whether an adjective, explicative apposition or emphasis, or a conjoined noun joined with al-; from this is the verse we are dealing with.
4- What is given, as a follower, what it would deserve if it were an independent vocative: this is the badal and the conjoined noun without al-; it takes ḍamma if it is single and the accusative if it is in construct.

dervis-irab:14-14.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مِنْسَأَتَهُ): al-minsaʾa is on the pattern mifʿala, a noun of instrument; it is the staff, because with it one drives away and puts back (yunsaʾ), like al-miknasa (broom), al-miksaḥa (sweeper) and al-miqʿaṣa. Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr and a group read منساته with an alif.

* I'rab:
(فَلَمَّا قَضَيْنا عَلَيْهِ الْمَوْتَ ما دَلَّهُمْ عَلى مَوْتِهِ إِلَّا دَابَّةُ الْأَرْضِ تَأْكُلُ مِنْسَأَتَهُ): the fāʾ is resumptive; لما is a temporal adverb (ẓarfiyya ḥīniyya), or a linking particle including the sense of condition. The clause قضينا is the muḍāf ilayhi of the adverb on the first view; نا is the fāʿil (agent); عليه is attached (mutaʿalliq) to قضينا; الموت is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ما is negative; دلهم is a past verb and a mafʿūl bihi; على موته is attached to دلهم; إلا is a particle of restriction; دابة الأرض is the fāʿil of دلهم; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to لما on both views. دابة الأرض is the little creature called al-saraqa [Translator's note: so in the source; the creature usually named here is al-araḍa, the termite, as the following sentence shows], and it was annexed to it [i.e. al-arḍ]; one says أرضت الخشبة أرضا when the termite (al-araḍa) has eaten it. The clause تأكل منسأته is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of دابة الأرض.
(فَلَمَّا خَرَّ تَبَيَّنَتِ الْجِنُّ أَنْ لَوْ كانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ الْغَيْبَ ما لَبِثُوا فِي الْعَذابِ الْمُهِينِ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; لما has been discussed just above. خرّ is a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "هو", referring to Solomon. The clause تبينت الجن is the answer to لما, with no grammatical position. أن is lightened from the heavy [أنّ], and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); لو is conditional; the clause كانوا is the khabar (predicate) of أن. أن and what falls within its scope is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) of الجن, in the manner of your saying "Zayd's ignorance became clear". Abū al-Baqāʾ took it as a badal of something omitted, i.e. the matter of the jinn became clear, namely that if they had known the unseen…; he also allowed أن with its ṣila to be in the position of the accusative, i.e. the jinn perceived their ignorance. There is nothing to prevent these two constructions. The clause يعلمون الغيب is the khabar of كانوا; the clause ما لبثوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of لو; في العذاب is attached to لبثوا, and المهين is an adjective of العذاب.

* Benefits:
The commentators have expatiated on the story of Solomon's death in a way that would take us beyond the scope of our book, but we cite some of what has been said about دابة الأرض because of its connection with language. What they have cited can be summarised in two views. The more apparent of them is what we gave earlier in the Rhetoric section [Translator's note: so in the source; it was given above in the I'rab section], namely that it is the little creature that eats wood. In al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj:
«Al-dābba is any animal that creeps (dabba), and it is predominantly applied to what is ridden; it applies to the masculine too. The Beast of the Earth (dābbat al-arḍ) is among the signs of the Hour, or the first of them. It will come out at Mecca from Mount al-Ṣafā, which will split open for it while the people are travelling to Minā — or from al-Ṭāʾif, or in three places three times. With it will be the staff of Moses and the seal of Solomon, upon them be peace. It will strike the believer with the staff and stamp the face of the disbeliever with the seal, so that there is engraved on it: this is a disbeliever». The second view is that al-arḍ is the maṣdar of your saying أرضت الدابة الخشبة تأرضها أرضا [the creature ate the wood], with fatḥa on the second radical of the maṣdar [i.e. al-araḍ]; Ibn ʿAbbās and al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Faḍl read it so. The discussion of the vowel of the second radical of the triliteral faʿl has been given before, so renew your acquaintance with it.

dervis-irab:15-19.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْعَرِمِ): We have found no word over which the commentators have differed as they have over this word. Therefore we shall cite the views we select and then proceed to weigh between them. We begin with what the author of al-Qāmūs mentioned. He said under the entry ʿurām: «ʿUrām of an army: its sharpness, its force and its numbers. Of bones and trees: the stripped bone (al-ʿurāq), and what falls of the bark of the boxthorn. Of a man: viciousness and harm. ʿarama — like naṣara, ḍaraba, karuma and ʿalima — ʿarāma and ʿurāman, with ḍamma, so he is ʿārim and ʿarim: he became fierce; the boy [ʿarama] against us: he was insolent and frolicsome, or arrogant, or he became corrupt. A day that is ʿārim: extreme in cold. ʿarama the bone: he stripped off the meat on it, like taʿarramahu; the boy ʿarama his mother: he sucked her; the camels ʿaramat the trees: they cropped them; ʿarama so-and-so: he struck him with ferocity. ʿarima the bone, like fariḥa: it became weak. Al-ʿaram, with fatḥas, and al-ʿurma, with ḍamma: black mixed with white in anything whatsoever, or it is a speckling with both without any spot becoming large; and whiteness at the lips (bi-maramma) of the sheep; he is aʿram and she is ʿarmāʾ, and the eggs of the sand-grouse are ʿurm. Al-ʿarmāʾ is the speckled snake. Al-aʿram: the multicoloured, the piebald; a flock of sheep and goats; the uncircumcised; the plural is ʿurmān and the plural of the plural ʿarāmīn. Al-ʿarama, with fatḥas: the smell of cooking; a threshed heap not yet winnowed; a gathering of sand; and a hard land bordering al-Dahnāʾ, facing ʿĀriḍ al-Yamāma. And, like fariḥa [i.e. al-ʿarima]: a dam by which a valley is blocked; its plural is ʿarim; or it is a plural without a singular; or it is the reservoirs built in valleys; the male rat; heavy rain; and a valley. By each of these His words, the Exalted, سيل العرم have been interpreted». Al-Jalāl chose that al-ʿarim is the plural of ʿarima, which is a structure or the like that holds back water until the time it is needed; this is what we today call dams, and it is the best interpretation of the verse. The cracking and collapse of dams can happen for various reasons.
(ذَواتا): the dual of ذوات or ذات. The word ذوات is singular, because its origin is ذوية, the wāw being the second radical and the yāʾ the third, since it is the feminine of ذو, and ذو was originally ذوى. When the yāʾ was vowelled and what preceded it had fatḥa, it was changed into alif, so it became ذوات; then the wāw was dropped for lightness. So when its dual is intended, one may look at its wording and say ذاتان, or look at its origin and say ذواتان.
Moreover, ذات is the feminine of ذو, its dual is ذواتان and its plural ذوات, and the feminine, dual and plural are inflected as their counterparts among singular, dual and plural nouns. One says: I met him ذات يوم or ذات ليلة or ذات مرة, i.e. on some day, at some time. That was ذات العويم, i.e. last year. He sat ذات اليمين, i.e. on the right. I met him أول ذات يدين, i.e. first of all. ذات الصدر: thought, or the secret. ذات اليمين, i.e. its side. ذات البين: the state; one says: set right ذات بينكم, i.e. your state upon which you come together. ذات شفة: a word; one says: I spoke to him and he did not answer me ذات شفة. ذات اليد: what you own; one says: ذات يده became little, i.e. what his hand owned. One says: the hen cast out ذات بطنها, i.e. laid eggs or voided. ذات الجنب among physicians: an inflammation occurring in the covering of the lung, from which arise coughing, fever and a stabbing in the side; ذات الرئة, ذات الصدر and ذات الكبد are ailments in these. Al-dhāt is also: that which is fit to be known and spoken about. ذات الشيء: its self, its essence and its substance. Ism al-dhāt (concrete noun) among the grammarians is what is applied to an entity, like man and lion; its counterpart is ism al-maʿnā (abstract noun), like knowledge and courage. Al-dhawāt among the post-classical writers (al-muwalladūn):
the notables of the people.
(أُكُلٍ خَمْطٍ): al-ukul, with two ḍammas, and al-ukl, with ḍamma and sukūn: fruit, or what is eaten. Al-khamṭ is the bitter and the sour; one says خمر خمطة: sour wine, and لبن خامض [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably خامط]:
sharp, changed. In al-Mukhtār: «al-khamṭ is a kind of arāk (toothbrush tree) that has fruit which is eaten». From Abū ʿUbayda: «every thorny tree». Al-Zajjāj said: «every plant that has taken on a taste of bitterness so that it cannot be eaten».
(أَثْلٍ): al-athla is the samura (acacia); it is said to be a tree of the ʿiḍāh (thorny trees), tall, with straight wood, from which bowls and cups are made. So it occurs figuratively in their saying:
نحت أثلته (he whittled his athla), when he disparages him; and so-and-so's athla is not whittled. Al-Aʿshā said:
ألست منتهيا عن نحت أثلتنا ... ولست ضائرها ما أطّت الإبل
(Will you not desist from whittling at our tree-trunk? You will not harm it as long as camels groan.)
So-and-so has an athla of wealth, i.e. a root of wealth; then they said أثّلت مالا and تأثلته (I acquired firmly-rooted wealth), and nobility that is muʾaththal and athīl (deep-rooted).
(سِدْرٍ): al-sidr is the lote tree (nabq), whose fruit is pleasant to eat, and for that reason it is planted in orchards. It is said that al-sidr is of two kinds: a kind whose fruit is eaten and whose leaves are used for washing the hands, and a kind having a fresh fruit that is not eaten at all, which is al-ḍāl.

* I'rab:
(لَقَدْ كانَ لِسَبَإٍ فِي مَسْكَنِهِمْ آيَةٌ): the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of realisation; كان is a defective past verb; لسبأ is its fronted khabar (predicate); في مسكنهم is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of سبأ, i.e. while they were in their dwelling; آية is the postponed noun of كان. Sabaʾ was discussed in detail in Sūrat al-Naml, so renew your acquaintance with it.
(جَنَّتانِ عَنْ يَمِينٍ وَشِمالٍ): جنتان is a badal (substitute) of آية, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject) whose implied form is "the sign is two gardens"; عن يمين وشمال is an adjective of جنتان. It appears that في means "at", for the dwellings were surrounded by the two gardens, not contained in them.
(كُلُوا مِنْ رِزْقِ رَبِّكُمْ وَاشْكُرُوا لَهُ بَلْدَةٌ طَيِّبَةٌ وَرَبٌّ غَفُورٌ): the clause is the quoted speech (maqūl al-qawl) of an omitted verb of saying, i.e. it was said to them by the tongue of circumstance or by the tongue of speech. كلوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); what is meant by this command is permission. من رزق ربكم is attached (mutaʿalliq) to كلوا. بلدة is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, meaning: this land is a good land; طيبة is an adjective. ورب غفور is conjoined to what precedes, i.e. and your Lord who provided for you and asked for your thanks is a forgiving Lord.
(فَأَعْرَضُوا فَأَرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ سَيْلَ الْعَرِمِ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; أعرضوا is a past verb and its fāʿil, and what it is attached to is omitted, i.e. from thanking Him. فأرسلنا is conjoined to فأعرضوا; عليهم is attached to أرسلنا; سيل العرم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
(وَبَدَّلْناهُمْ بِجَنَّتَيْهِمْ جَنَّتَيْنِ ذَواتَيْ أُكُلٍ خَمْطٍ وَأَثْلٍ وَشَيْءٍ مِنْ سِدْرٍ قَلِيلٍ): وبدلناهم: the wāw is a conjunction; بدلناهم is a past verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; بجنتهم is attached to بدلناهم; جنتين is the second mafʿūl bihi; ذواتى is an adjective; أكل is the muḍāf ilayhi; خمط is an adjective, as if it were said: an unpleasant fruit. It was also read with annexation. The wording of Abū al-Baqāʾ: «أكل خمط: it is read with tanwīn, and the implied form is أكل أكل خمط (fruit of the fruit of khamṭ), the muḍāf being omitted because al-khamṭ is a tree and al-ukul is its fruit. It is said that the implied form is أكل ذي خمط; and it is said that it is a badal of it, khamṭ being made the fruit because of its proximity to it and its being the cause of it. It is also read with annexation, which is clear». أثل is conjoined to أكل, and شيء is also conjoined; من سدر is an adjective of شيء and قليل a second adjective.
(ذلِكَ جَزَيْناهُمْ بِما كَفَرُوا وَهَلْ نُجازِي إِلَّا الْكَفُورَ): ذلك is the second object of جزيناهم, put before it, because it takes two objects, i.e. We recompensed them with that exchange. جزيناهم is a past verb, its fāʿil and first mafʿūl bihi; بما is attached to جزيناهم; the bāʾ is causal and ما is maṣdarī, i.e. because of their patience (صبرهم) [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense requires كفرهم, "their disbelief"]. هل is an interrogative particle in the sense of negation; نجازي is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "نحن"; إلا is a particle of restriction; الكفور is a mafʿūl bihi.
(وَجَعَلْنا بَيْنَهُمْ وَبَيْنَ الْقُرَى الَّتِي بارَكْنا فِيها قُرىً ظاهِرَةً): the wāw is a conjunction; جعلنا is a verb and its fāʿil; بينهم: the adverb is attached to an omitted second object of جعلنا; وبين القرى is conjoined to بينهم; التي is an adjective of القرى; the clause باركنا فيها is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; قرى is the first mafʿūl bihi and ظاهرة a naʿt (adjective). The clause is conjoined to what precedes it, as a story conjoined to a story: He mentioned first the blessing of the two gardens that He lavished upon them, then their exchange as mentioned above, then His making their lands separated and scattered after they had been connected and united.
(وَقَدَّرْنا فِيهَا السَّيْرَ سِيرُوا فِيها لَيالِيَ وَأَيَّاماً آمِنِينَ): وقدرنا: the wāw is a conjunction; قدرنا is a past verb and its fāʿil; فيها is attached to قدرنا or to السير; السير is a mafʿūl bihi. The clause سيروا is in the position of the accusative as the quoted speech of an omitted verb of saying; فيها is attached to سيروا; ليالي and أياما are two adverbs also attached to سيروا; آمنين is a ḥāl. Al-Qurṭubī's parsing of ليالي and أياما did not seem sound to us, for he said that they are accusative as ḥāls. The secret of their being indefinite will come in the Rhetoric section.
(فَقالُوا رَبَّنا باعِدْ بَيْنَ أَسْفارِنا وَظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ فَجَعَلْناهُمْ أَحادِيثَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; قالوا is a verb and its fāʿil; ربنا is a vocative in construct from which the vocative particle has been omitted; باعد is an imperative verb; بين is an adverb attached to باعد, and أسفارنا is the muḍāf ilayhi. ظلموا is conjoined to فقالوا, and أنفسهم is an object. That was because they became insolent and sated with the good life and the ease of their state, so they sought toil, fatigue and moving about the lands. فجعلناهم is conjoined to ظلموا أنفسهم, and أحاديث is the second mafʿūl bihi of جعلناهم.
(وَمَزَّقْناهُمْ كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ شَكُورٍ): ومزقناهم is also conjoined, and كل ممزق is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. We dispersed them with a dispersal after which there is no reunion. Al-Shaʿbī said: «The Anṣār went to Yathrib, Ghassān to Syria, al-Azd to ʿUmān and Khuzāʿa to Tihāma, and the Arabs used to make them a proverb, saying: they scattered like the hands of Sabaʾ (تفرقوا أيادي سبأ)». The meaning of this proverb and its parsing were given in al-Naml, so renew your acquaintance with it. إن is a particle resembling the verb; في ذلك is its fronted khabar; [then] the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); آيات is its postponed noun; لكل صبار is an adjective of آيات, and شكور is an adjective of صبار.

* Rhetoric:
1- Mushākala (verbal correspondence):
In His words «جنتين» there is the device of mushākala, which, as explained before, is mentioning something by the word for something else because it occurs in its company. He called the replacement "two gardens" for the sake of mushākala, and there is in it a kind of sarcasm at them. Abū Tammām said:
والدهر ألأم من شرقت بلؤمه ... إلا إذا أشرقته بكريم
(Time is the meanest one whose meanness you choke on — except when you make it choke on a noble man.)
i.e. you confined it with a noble man [Translator's note: so in the source], so he said أشرقته by way of mushākala.
2- Indefiniteness:
In the indefiniteness of ليالي and أياما there is an allusion to the shortness of their journeys; they were short because they were grazing in the midst of an ample and comfortable life, not needing continuous toil nor bearing the hardship of journeys to obtain what would make their life easy.
3- Tadhyīl (tail-piece confirmation):
In His words «ذلك جزيناهم» (the verse) there is the device of tadhyīl, whose discussion has also been given before. It is of two kinds. The first is what runs as a proverb, and its discussion has also been given before. The second is what does not take the form of a proverb, namely that the second clause depends on the first in conveying the intended meaning, i.e. is that specific recompense dealt out [to anyone but the ungrateful]? The content of the first clause is that Allah the Exalted recompensed the people of Sabaʾ for their disbelief, and the content of the second is that that specific punishment befalls only the ungrateful. There is a difference between our saying "I recompensed him because of such-and-such" and our saying "that recompense is given only to one in whom that cause is found". Because they differ, it is valid to make the second a reason for the first; but the difference in their concepts does not preclude one of them emphasising the other, because of an entailment of meaning.

dervis-irab:20-22.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ صَدَّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِبْلِيسُ ظَنَّهُ فَاتَّبَعُوهُ إِلَّا فَرِيقاً مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): the wāw conjoins to what precedes, or is resumptive; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of realisation; صدق is a past verb; عليهم is attached (mutaʿalliq) to صدق; إبليس is its fāʿil (agent) and ظنه its object — as though he formed an opinion about them and promised himself [something], and then made it come true. صدق was also read without doubling, with the same meaning, so that ظنه is accusative by removal of the preposition; it may also be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). It was read with إبليس in the accusative as the object and ظنه in the nominative as the agent; and it was read with both in the nominative, ظنه being a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) of إبليس. فاتبعوه: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and اتبعوه is a past verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi. The statement may be specific, so that the pronoun refers to the people of Sabaʾ, or general, so that the pronoun refers to the children of Adam. إلا is a particle of exception; فريقا is the excepted, which may be disjoined (munqaṭiʿ) or joined (muttaṣil); من المؤمنين is an adjective of فريقا.
(وَما كانَ لَهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ سُلْطانٍ): the wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; كان is a defective past verb; له is its fronted khabar (predicate); عليهم is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of سلطان. من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and سلطان is genitive in wording and, in position, the postponed noun of ليس [Translator's note: so in the source; the verb in the verse is كان].
(إِلَّا لِنَعْلَمَ مَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِالْآخِرَةِ مِمَّنْ هُوَ مِنْها فِي شَكٍّ): إلا is a particle of restriction; the lām is causal — it is said to be of consequence — and the exception is "emptied" (mufarragh) from the most general of reasons, so it is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). نعلم is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām. من may be interrogative, standing in place of the two objects of knowing, in which case it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause يؤمن بالآخرة its khabar. It may also be relative, in the position of the accusative as the object of نعلم, and this is preferable; the clause يؤمن is the ṣila (relative clause), and بالآخرة is attached to يؤمن. ممن is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نعلم, because it includes the sense of "We distinguish". هو is a mubtadaʾ; منها is a ḥāl because it was originally an adjective of شك; في شك is the khabar, and the clause is the ṣila.
(وَرَبُّكَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ حَفِيظٌ): ربك is a mubtadaʾ; على كل شيء is attached to حفيظ; حفيظ is the khabar of ربك.
(قُلِ ادْعُوا الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ): قل is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, given kasra to avoid the meeting of two vowelless letters. The clause ادعوا الذين is the quoted speech (maqūl al-qawl); the clause زعمتم is the ṣila; من دون الله is an adjective of the omitted second object, and the first object is also omitted, the implied form being زعمتوهم آلهة (you claimed them to be gods). The first was omitted because of the length of the relative noun with its ṣila, and the second was omitted because its adjective, namely من دون الله, stands in its place. This is among the most remarkable and most emphatic of speech. We quote for you al-Zamakhsharī's wording on this point in full. He said: «If you ask: where are the two objects of زعم? I say: one of them is the omitted pronoun referring from it back to the relative noun. As for the second, it must be either من دون الله, or لا يملكون, or omitted. The first is not valid, because your saying "they are besides Allah" does not cohere as a sentence; nor the second, because they did not claim that, so how would they speak what is an argument against them, and what, if they said it, would be saying what is true and is the affirmation of Oneness? So it remains that it is omitted, its implied form being: you claimed them to be gods besides Allah. The pronoun referring to the relative was omitted, as it was omitted in His words: أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا, for lightness, because of the length of the relative noun with its ṣila; and آلهة was omitted because it is a qualified noun whose adjective is من دون الله, and the qualified noun may be omitted with the adjective put in its place when it is understood. So the two objects of زعم are both omitted, for two different reasons».
(لا يَمْلِكُونَ مِثْقالَ ذَرَّةٍ فِي السَّماواتِ وَلا فِي الْأَرْضِ): the clause is a ḥāl of those you claimed to be gods; you may make it resumptive, introduced to explain their state. لا is negative; يملكون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; مثقال ذرة is a mafʿūl bihi; في السموات والأرض is attached to يملكون or to an omitted ḥāl.
(وَما لَهُمْ فِيهِما مِنْ شِرْكٍ وَما لَهُ مِنْهُمْ مِنْ ظَهِيرٍ): the wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; لهم is a fronted khabar; فيهما is a ḥāl; من is a redundant preposition; شرك is genitive in wording and nominative in position, as a postponed mubtadaʾ, or as the noun of ما on the view of those who allow its khabar to precede its noun. The wāw is also a conjunction; ما is negative; له is a fronted khabar; منهم is a ḥāl; من ظهير is a postponed mubtadaʾ, as before.

dervis-irab:23-27.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فُزِّعَ عَنْ قُلُوبِهِمْ): in the passive. فزّع عنه, with doubling: he removed fear from him. Al-fazaʿ, with two fatḥas: terror, fear, and also rescuing. In al-Asās:
«فزع عن قلبه: fear was lifted from it». So the doubling here is privative, as one says:
قرّدت البعير, i.e. I removed its ticks (qurād).

* I'rab:
(وَلا تَنْفَعُ الشَّفاعَةُ عِنْدَهُ إِلَّا لِمَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ): the statement is resumptive, introduced to explain the destiny in which the intercession of intercessors will not avail except for one for whom the Pen has already written permission. لا is negative; تنفع الشفاعة is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); عنده is an adverb attached (mutaʿalliq) to تنفع or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); إلا is a particle of restriction; لمن is attached to الشفاعة, since one says شفعت له, or to تنفع. Al-Zamakhsharī has a subtle discussion of what this lām is attached to, which we cite in full. He said: «You say الشفاعة لزيد in the sense that he is the intercessor, as you say:
الكرم لزيد (generosity belongs to Zayd); and in the sense that he is the one interceded for, as you say: القيام لزيد (rising is for Zayd). So His words ولا تنفع الشفاعة عنده إلا لمن أذن له may be on either of these two views, i.e. intercession does not avail except as belonging to whoever among the intercessors has been given permission and has been licensed for it; or intercession does not avail except as being for one for whom permission has been given, i.e. for his intercessor. Or it is the second lām in your saying أذن لزيد لعمرو, i.e. for his sake; as if it were said: except for one for whose sake permission was given to the intercessor. This is a subtle view, and it is the [correct] view». أذن is an active past verb, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), referring to Allah; له is attached to أذن. أذن was also read in the passive.
(حَتَّى إِذا فُزِّعَ عَنْ قُلُوبِهِمْ): حتى is a particle of limit and genitive, and the limit is for something omitted understood from the context of speech, as if it were said: they wait and halt (يتوفقون [Translator's note: so in the source; read يتوقفون]), bewildered, stunned and afraid, fears besetting them and doubts tossing them about — will permission be given them or not? — until, when [fear] is removed. فزع is passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is the preposition and its genitive noun, i.e. عن قلوبهم. It was also read in the active, in which case the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to it, i.e. Allah removed [fear] from their hearts.
(قالُوا ماذا قالَ رَبُّكُمْ قالُوا الْحَقَّ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْكَبِيرُ): قالوا is the apodosis of إذا. ما is an interrogative noun and ذا a relative noun as the khabar (predicate); the clause is the quoted speech of قال, put before it. قال ربكم is a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the quoted speech of the first قالوا. [The second] قالوا is a verb and its fāʿil; الحق is accusative by an implied verb of saying, i.e. our Lord said the true word; you may parse القول [i.e. the implied word] as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), with الحق as an adjective. هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject), العلي a first khabar and الكبير a second khabar; this is the completion of the intercessors' speech.
(قُلْ مَنْ يَرْزُقُكُمْ مِنَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ قُلِ اللَّهُ): قل is an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is latent, referring to the Messenger, as a rebuke to the polytheists and to compel them to confess their impotence. من is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and the clause يرزقكم is the khabar; من السموات is attached to يرزقكم, and الأرض is conjoined to السموات. قل is an imperative verb; الله is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. Allah provides for us; or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. He is Allah.
(وَإِنَّا أَوْ إِيَّاكُمْ لَعَلى هُدىً أَوْ فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ): the wāw is a conjunction; إن and its noun; أو إياكم: a detached pronoun conjoined to the noun of إن; [then] the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); على هدى is the khabar of إن. أو is a conjunction in its usual sense according to the Basrans, and is not for doubt; more discussion of this construction will come in the Rhetoric section. أو في ضلال is conjoined to His words لعلى هدى, and مبين is an adjective.
(قُلْ: لا تُسْئَلُونَ عَمَّا أَجْرَمْنا وَلا نُسْئَلُ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ): لا is negative; تسألون is a passive imperfect verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; عما is attached to تسألون; ما is relative or maṣdarī; أجرمنا is a verb and its fāʿil. ولا نسأل عما تعملون is conjoined to لا تسألون عما أجرمنا. Further discussion of it will also come in the Rhetoric section.
(قُلْ يَجْمَعُ بَيْنَنا رَبُّنا ثُمَّ يَفْتَحُ بَيْنَنا بِالْحَقِّ وَهُوَ الْفَتَّاحُ الْعَلِيمُ): the clause يجمع is the quoted speech; بيننا is an adverb attached to يجمع; ربنا is the fāʿil of يجمع; ثم يفتح بيننا is conjoined to what precedes; بالحق is a ḥāl; هو is a mubtadaʾ, الفتاح a first khabar and العليم a second khabar.
(قُلْ أَرُونِيَ الَّذِينَ أَلْحَقْتُمْ بِهِ شُرَكاءَ): أروني is an imperative verb; the wāw is the fāʿil, the nūn is the nūn of protection, and the yāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi, because the seeing is cognitive, transitive to two objects before the transfer; when the hamza of transfer was added, it became transitive to three. الذين is a relative noun, the second mafʿūl bihi of أروني; the clause ألحقتم is the ṣila (relative clause), and the referent pronoun is omitted, i.e. ألحقتموهم, and it is the second object; به is attached to ألحقتم; شركاء is the third mafʿūl bihi of أروني. The seeing may also be visual, transitive to one object before the transfer; when the hamza of transfer was added, it became transitive to two, the first being the yāʾ of the speaker and the second the relative noun, and شركاء is accusative as a ḥāl of the omitted referent pronoun, i.e. show me those joined to Him, as partners. The meaning of the command here will come in the Rhetoric section.
(كَلَّا بَلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ): كلا is a particle of deterrence and rebuke; بل is a particle of digression (iḍrāb); هو is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), a mubtadaʾ; الله is a second mubtadaʾ, and العزيز الحكيم are its two khabars, the clause being the khabar of هو. You may make هو a pronoun referring to Allah and parse it as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is الله, with العزيز الحكيم as two adjectives.

* Rhetoric:
These verses abound in kinds of rhetoric, which we summarise as follows:
1- Al-farāʾid (unique gems):
In His words «حتى إذا فزع عن قلوبهم» there is an original device called al-farāʾid: the speaker brings into his speech a word that stands like the unique gem among the beads of a necklace — the jewel that has no equal — such that if it were dropped from the speech nothing else could take its place. Examples of it have already passed. In the expression فزع عن قلوبهم there is a rarity of eloquence that cannot be surpassed. Among the examples of this device in poetry is the saying of Abū Tammām:
ومعترك للشوق أهدى به الهوى ... إلى ذي الهوى نجل العيون ربائبا
(And many a battlefield of longing in which passion presented to the lover wide-eyed, carefully reared beauties.)
The unique gem is in the word معترك (battlefield). Shaykh ʿUmar ibn al-Fāriḍ borrowed it and said:
ما بين معترك الأحداق والمهج ... أنا القتيل بلا إثم ولا حرج
(Between the battlefield of eyes and hearts, I am the slain, without sin or blame.)
2- Al-istidrāj (drawing the opponent on):
In His words «وإنا أو إياكم لعلى هدى أو في ضلال مبين». This is a device regarded as the very axis around which rhetoric turns, because it draws the opponent on and compels him to submit and concede and to give up obstinacy and wrangling. When He had established the proof against them, He addressed them with the fair-minded speech of which whoever hears it says to the one addressed: your companion has been fair to you. Similar is a man's saying to his companion: "[It is] from me or from you, and one of us is surely lying." From it is the saying of the poet Ḥassān ibn Thābit:
أتهجوه ولست له بكفء ... فشر كما لخير كما الفداء
(Do you lampoon him when you are no match for him? May the worse of you two be ransom for the better of you two.)
It is from a long ode in which he lampooned Abū Sufyān before his conversion to Islam. The hamza is the interrogative of rebuke and the wāw is circumstantial, i.e. that is not fitting. شر and خير are of the type of the elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl), and they are distinguished by dropping their hamza for lightness, owing to their frequent use; but what is meant by them here is the basic quality, not its excess. The worse is Abū Sufyān, and the clause is an imprecation: he prayed against him that he be a ransom for the Messenger of Allah, and he presented it in the form of ambiguity for the sake of fairness in speech. Therefore, when those present heard it, they said: this is the fairest verse the Arabs have composed.
3- Variation in the particles:
In this verse there is a variation between the two prepositions. They were varied in their application to truth and falsehood only because the one in the right is as if mounted on a fine horse, galloping with it wherever he wishes, while the one in falsehood is as if
sunk in darkness, low down in it, not knowing which way to turn. This is a subtle meaning; seldom is its like observed in speech. Often we have heard a man blaming his brother or reproaching his friend over something say to him: "You are on (ʿalā) your old error, as I have known you", using على in the place of في. Although this is permissible, the use of «في» here is preferable for the reason we have indicated. The explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya) is clear, and it has been discussed elsewhere.
4- The meaning of the command:
His words «أروني»: He commanded them to show Him the idols although they were within His sight, in order to expose their error and make them see the falsity of their opinion.

dervis-irab:28-33.t:
* I'rab:
(وَما أَرْسَلْناكَ إِلَّا كَافَّةً لِلنَّاسِ بَشِيراً وَنَذِيراً وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; ما is negative; أرسلناك is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); إلا is a particle of restriction. كافة is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the kāf in أرسلناك, or of الناس, i.e. to all people, on the view of those who allow the ḥāl to precede the preposition and its genitive noun; or it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. a sending that embraces all people. More discussion of «كافة» will come in the Benefits section, and it is an enjoyable discussion. للناس is an adjective of كافة, or [attached] to كافة. بشيرا and نذيرا are two ḥāls of the kāf. لكن is a particle resembling the verb; أكثر الناس is its noun, and the clause لا يعلمون its khabar (predicate).
(وَيَقُولُونَ مَتى هذَا الْوَعْدُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; يقولون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; متى is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as an adverb, and this adverb is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted fronted khabar; هذا is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and الوعد is a badal (substitute). إن is conditional; كنتم is a defective past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the tāʾ is its noun and صادقين its khabar; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.
(قُلْ لَكُمْ مِيعادُ يَوْمٍ لا تَسْتَأْخِرُونَ عَنْهُ ساعَةً وَلا تَسْتَقْدِمُونَ): لكم is a fronted khabar and ميعاد يوم a postponed mubtadaʾ; it is a maṣdar annexed to the adverb. The clause لا تستأخرون is an adjective of يوم or of ميعاد; عنه is attached to تستأخرون; ساعة is an adverb also attached to تستأخرون; ولا تستقدمون is conjoined to لا تستأخرون.
(وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا: لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ بِهذَا الْقُرْآنِ وَلا بِالَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ): قال الذين is a verb and its fāʿil; the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause). لن is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity; نؤمن is an imperfect verb, accusative by لن, and the clause is the quoted speech (maqūl al-qawl). بهذا is attached to نؤمن, and القرآن is a badal; ولا بالذي is conjoined to بهذا القرآن; بين is an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila of الذي, and يديه is the muḍāf ilayhi of the adverb. What is meant by what is "between the hands" of the Qurʾān is the books of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that preceded it.
(وَلَوْ تَرى إِذِ الظَّالِمُونَ مَوْقُوفُونَ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ يَرْجِعُ بَعْضُهُمْ إِلى بَعْضٍ الْقَوْلَ): لو is conditional; ترى is a nominative imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنت"; it is the protasis, and the apodosis is omitted, i.e. you would have seen the most astonishing wonder, or you would have seen a stunning state. إذ is an adverb of past time attached to ترى. الظالمون is a mubtadaʾ and موقوفون its khabar, i.e. detained; it is the plural of موقوف, the passive participle of the transitive triliteral وقف. In al-Miṣbāḥ the following is found: «وقفت الدابة تقف وقفا ووقوفا: it stood still; and I stopped it (وقفتها) — it is both transitive and intransitive. وقفت الرجل عن الشيء وقفا: I held him back from it». عند ربهم is an adverb attached to موقوفون. The clause يرجع is a ḥāl of the pronoun in موقوفون; بعضهم is the fāʿil; إلى بعض is attached to يرجع; القول is the mafʿūl bihi of يرجع, because it is transitive.
(يَقُولُ الَّذِينَ اسْتُضْعِفُوا لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا): the clause يقول is explicative of يرجع, so it has no grammatical position. الذين is the fāʿil of يقول; the clause استضعفوا is the ṣila; للذين is attached to يقول, and the clause استكبروا is the ṣila.
(لَوْلا أَنْتُمْ لَكُنَّا مُؤْمِنِينَ): لولا is a particle of non-occurrence due to existence; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is necessarily omitted, i.e. existing. The lām links the apodosis of لولا; the clause كنا مؤمنين has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; كان and its noun, and مؤمنين its khabar.
(قالَ الَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا لِلَّذِينَ اسْتُضْعِفُوا): قال الذين is a verb and its fāʿil; the clause استكبروا is the ṣila; للذين is attached to قال; the clause استضعفوا is the ṣila, and it is passive; the clause is resumptive.
(أَنَحْنُ صَدَدْناكُمْ عَنِ الْهُدى بَعْدَ إِذْ جاءَكُمْ بَلْ كُنْتُمْ مُجْرِمِينَ): the hamza is the interrogative of disapproval, as though they denied that they were the ones who committed the offence of turning them away from faith. نحن is a mubtadaʾ and the clause صددناكم the khabar; عن الهدى is attached to صددناكم; بعد is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it occurs after a definite noun. إذ is an adverb annexed to its like, by extension in the usage of adverbs; it is also said that إذ means the maṣdarī أن, and that is what is understood from al-Zamakhsharī's interpretation. The clause جاءكم is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. بل is a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction; كنتم is a defective past verb, the tāʾ is its noun and مجرمين its khabar.
(وَقالَ الَّذِينَ اسْتُضْعِفُوا لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا): its parsing has been given. The conjunction is retained here, while it was dropped in the preceding clause, because this is another statement of the oppressed.
(بَلْ مَكْرُ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهارِ): بل is a particle of digression; مكر الليل is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. the plotting of night and day turned us away; or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. the cause of our disbelief is the plotting of night and day. The annexation of plotting to night and day is of the type of figurative attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī), parallels of which have passed; it is a maṣdar annexed to its nominative [agent]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «The meaning of مكر الليل والنهار is your plotting in the night and the day; the adverb was treated with latitude by being treated like the mafʿūl bihi, and the plotting annexed to it; or their night and day were made plotters by way of figurative attribution». The root sense of al-makr in the speech of the Arabs is deception and stratagem.
(إِذْ تَأْمُرُونَنا أَنْ نَكْفُرَ بِاللَّهِ وَنَجْعَلَ لَهُ أَنْداداً): the adverb is attached to مكر; the clause تأمروننا is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. أن and what falls within its scope is accusative by removal of the preposition, attached to تأمروننا. نجعل is conjoined to نكفر; له is a ḥāl because it was originally an adjective of أندادا; أندادا is a mafʿūl bihi. The preposition and its genitive noun may also be the second object of نجعل, with أندادا as the first object of نجعل.
(وَأَسَرُّوا النَّدامَةَ لَمَّا رَأَوُا الْعَذابَ): the wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; أسروا is a verb and its fāʿil; الندامة is a mafʿūl bihi. The pronoun refers to both groups, i.e. both groups concealed regret for the disbelief they had committed and hid it from others; or each of them hid it from the other for fear of gloating. لما is a temporal adverb attached to أسروا; the clause رأوا is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; العذاب is a mafʿūl bihi.
(وَجَعَلْنَا الْأَغْلالَ فِي أَعْناقِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): the wāw is a conjunction; جعلنا is a verb and its fāʿil; الأغلال is the first object of جعلنا, and في أعناق الذين كفروا its second object. The speech is of the type of inversion (al-qalb); the original is: and We put the necks of those who disbelieved in the shackles.
(هَلْ يُجْزَوْنَ إِلَّا ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ): the clause is a ḥāl of الذين كفروا. هل is an interrogative particle, the interrogative having the sense of negation; يجزون is a passive imperfect verb and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); إلا is a particle of restriction; ما is the second object of يجزون; the clause كانوا is the ṣila, and the clause يعملون is the khabar of كانوا.

* Benefits:
The basic rule for the ḥāl is that it comes after the one it describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl). It may optionally precede it, as in: جاء راكبا علي; and from this is the saying of Ṭarafa ibn al-ʿAbd:
فسقى ديارك غير مفسدها ... صوب الربيع وديمة تهمي
(May the downpour of spring and a steadily pouring rain water your abodes, without ruining them.)
It must precede it in two cases:
1- When the one it describes is an indefinite noun that does not fulfil the conditions, as in:
لعليّ مهذبا غلام; and the poet's saying: لمية موحشا طلل ... يلوح كأنه خلل
(Mayya has a deserted ruin that gleams like the lining of a sword-sheath.)
and the other's saying:
وفي الجسم مني بينا لو علمته ... شحوب وإن تستشهدي العين تشهد
(In my body, plainly, if you knew it, there is wasting; and if you call the eye to witness, it will testify.)
2- When it [the one described] is restricted by it, as in: ما جاء ناجحا إلا عليّ and إنما جاء ناجحا علي. You say that when you wish to restrict coming in a state of success to ʿAlī.
It must come after it in three cases:
1- When it [the ḥāl] is the restricted element, as in ما جاء خالد إلا ناجحا and إنما جاء خالد ناجحا. You say that when you wish to restrict Khālid's coming to the state of success. From this is His words, the Exalted, «وما نرسل المرسلين إلا مبشرين ومنذرين».
2- When the one it describes is genitive by annexation, as in يعجبني وقوف علي خطيبا and سرني عملك مخلصا. As for what is genitive by a genuine preposition, the majority forbade putting the ḥāl before it, so one does not say مررت راكبا بعلي or أخذت عاثرا بيد خليل. Al-Fārisī, Ibn Kaysān, Ibn Jinnī and others allowed putting it first. Ibn Mālik said: putting it first is correct, because it occurs in eloquent usage, as in His words, the Exalted, «وما أرسلناك إلا كافة للناس», for كافة is a ḥāl of the genitive noun, namely الناس, and it has preceded the genitive noun it describes; and as in the poet's saying: تسليت طرا عنكم بعد بينكم ... بذكراكم حتى كأنكم عندي
(I consoled myself entirely about you after your departure with remembrance of you, until it was as if you were with me.)
Those who forbid it said: the truth is that this verse is poetic licence, or طرا is a ḥāl of an omitted عنكم indicated by the عنكم that is mentioned; and كافة in the verse is a ḥāl of the kāf in أرسلناك, the tāʾ being for intensification, not for the feminine — al-Zajjāj said this. Ibn Mālik rejected it on the ground that adding the tāʾ for intensification is limited to what is heard, and generally occurs only in intensive patterns like علامة [Translator's note: the source has علاقة, presumably a misprint for علامة], and كافة is otherwise.
For further benefit, we cite views of some eminent scholars regarding the parsing of كافة. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «Whoever makes it a ḥāl of the genitive noun preceding it has erred, because putting the ḥāl of a genitive noun before it is, in impossibility, like putting the genitive noun before the preposition. How often we see someone commit such an error and then not be content with it until he adds to it making the lām mean إلى, and so commits both errors together».
Abū ʿAlī said: «Putting the ḥāl before the genitive noun it describes, and before what it is attached to, has occurred; and if it is permissible to put it before the one it describes and before what governs it, then putting it before the one it describes alone is more permissible».
Al-Fīrūzābādī, the author of al-Qāmūs, said: «جاء الناس كافة, i.e. all of them. One does not say جاءت الكافة, because al- does not enter it — al-Jawharī was mistaken — and it is not annexed». His commentator corrected him, saying in Tāj al-ʿArūs, in summary:
«The wording of al-Jawharī is: al-kāffa: the whole of people; one says: I met them كافة, i.e. all of them. As you see, there is no mistake in this, because an indefinite noun, when its wording is intended, may be made definite. What the author [of al-Qāmūs] mentioned is what the majority agree upon; al-Nawawī cited it in al-Tahdhīb and faulted the jurists for using it with al- or in annexation. Our shaykh said: what shows that al-Jawharī did not intend what the author attributed to him is that he gave only an example agreeing with the majority. Moreover, that saying of theirs was rejected by al-Shihāb in Sharḥ al-Durra, who held it correct that it is said, though rarely». Al-Shihāb al-Khafājī wrote at length in defence of adding al- to كافة and annexing it. The commentator of al-Lubāb said:
it has been used in the genitive, and he adduced as evidence the saying of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb: «I have assigned to the family of Banū Kāhila, upon the whole (كافة) of the house of the Muslims [Translator's note: so in the source; the usual wording is بيت مال المسلمين, "the treasury of the Muslims"], two hundred mithqāls of pure gold every year».

dervis-irab:34-37.t:
* I'rab:
(وَما أَرْسَلْنا فِي قَرْيَةٍ مِنْ نَذِيرٍ إِلَّا قالَ مُتْرَفُوها): a resumptive statement, introduced to console him ﷺ. وما أرسلنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); في قرية is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أرسلنا; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and نذير is genitive in wording and accusative in position as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). إلا is a particle of restriction; the clause قال مترفوها is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of قرية, even though it is indefinite, because it occurs in a context of negation. مترفوها is the fāʿil of قال, i.e. those living in luxury in it.
(إِنَّا بِما أُرْسِلْتُمْ بِهِ كافِرُونَ): the clause is the quoted speech (maqūl al-qawl) of their saying. إن and its noun; بما is attached to كافرون; ما is relative; the clause أرسلتم is the ṣila (relative clause); أرسلتم is passive and the tāʾ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); به is attached to أرسلتم; كافرون is the khabar (predicate) of إن. The implied form is: we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent.
(وَقالُوا نَحْنُ أَكْثَرُ أَمْوالًا وَأَوْلاداً وَما نَحْنُ بِمُعَذَّبِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; قالوا is a verb and its fāʿil; نحن is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and أكثر the khabar; أموالا is a tamyīz (specification), and أولادا is conjoined to أموالا. ما is Ḥijāzī [i.e. operating like ليس]; نحن is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and معذبين is genitive in wording and accusative in position as the khabar of ما.
(قُلْ إِنَّ رَبِّي يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ): إن and its noun, and the clause يبسط الرزق is its khabar; لمن is attached to يبسط; the clause يشاء is the ṣila; يقدر is conjoined to يبسط, and its meaning is: He straitens it.
(وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial; لكن and its noun, and the clause لا يعلمون is its khabar. The object of يعلمون is omitted, i.e. the wise reason behind that: He extends provision to the disobedient by way of leading them on step by step and granting respite, and straitens it for the obedient by way of testing and trial.
(وَما أَمْوالُكُمْ وَلا أَوْلادُكُمْ بِالَّتِي تُقَرِّبُكُمْ عِنْدَنا زُلْفى): the wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; ما is Ḥijāzī; أموالكم is its noun, and ولا أولادكم is conjoined to أموالكم. The bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and التي is genitive in wording and accusative in position as the khabar of ليس [Translator's note: so in the source; i.e. the khabar of ما, which operates like ليس]. Wealth and children are described with التي because the broken plural, whether of rational or non-rational beings, is treated as a feminine singular. The clause تقربكم is the ṣila; عندنا is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl; زلفى is a maṣdar from the meaning of the governing verb, so it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) according to the meaning, i.e. they bring you near with a nearness.
(إِلَّا مَنْ آمَنَ وَعَمِلَ صالِحاً): إلا means "but" (لكن), so the exception is disjoined (munqaṭiʿ), because the address is to the disbelievers, and whoever believes is not ranked among them; من is the excepted. It may also be joined (muttaṣil), excepted from the object in يقربكم. It may also be parsed as a mubtadaʾ, with what follows as the khabar. The clause آمن is the ṣila; عمل is conjoined to آمن; صالحا is a mafʿūl bihi, or a mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. righteous work.
(فَأُولئِكَ لَهُمْ جَزاءُ الضِّعْفِ بِما عَمِلُوا): the fāʾ is linking, because of the sense of condition in the relative noun. أولئك is a demonstrative and a mubtadaʾ; the reference is to من, and the plural is in view of its meaning, just as the singular of the two verbs is in view of its wording. لهم is a fronted khabar and جزاء الضعف a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the khabar of أولئك. The meaning of جزاء الضعف is that their single good deed is multiplied tenfold for them. The annexation is either the annexation of the maṣdar to its object, or the annexation of the qualified noun to its adjective; the meaning on the first is that Allah recompenses them with the multiple, and on the second: they have the multiplied recompense. بما is attached to جزاء; ما is relative or maṣdarī.
(وَهُمْ فِي الْغُرُفاتِ آمِنُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; هم is a mubtadaʾ; في الغرفات is a ḥāl or is attached to آمنون; آمنون is their khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «وما أموالكم ولا أولادكم» (the verse) there is iltifāt (shift) from the third person to direct address. The secret of it is emphasis in establishing the statement: that what you rejoice and delight in — the abundance of children and wealth — will not avail you in the slightest, nor bring you near to Us so long as you persist in your present state, indulging in answering the calls of error and misguidance. In this there is an implicit indication of spending wealth in the way of Allah and in the avenues of good, and of educating children and preparing them for what will set right their religion and their worldly life. Al-zulfā is nearness (al-qurbā), and al-zulfa is a drawing near (al-qurba).
